data_info.detail: CCTS annual reports supply provider counts and outcome rates. Local files add the issue detail from its downloadable workbooks.

readme.note: Compare Rogers in 2023–24 with the Rogers/Shaw entry in 2024–25, where the published accepted count was 6,485. Open a complaint issues workbook to filter by provider, province and service and count distinct complaints separately from issue rows.

title: PIPEDA Findings
description: Search published Canadian privacy investigations, compare issue-level findings and save citations to the original records.

data_info.detail: The federal Privacy Commissioner’s business investigations catalogue supplies publication dates, document types and original decisions.

readme.note: Search for Bell and open report 2026-003. Its access-response deadline, cellphone-log procedures and openness issue have separate conclusions. The record gives both the findings date and the publication date.

title: Grid Dark
description: Compare power restoration bulletins with regional internet measurements during two Canadian storms.

data_info.detail: Utility bulletins supply dated customer counts. Georgia Tech IODA measurements show how the provincial internet signal compared with its preceding week.

readme.note: During Fiona, Nova Scotia’s lowest hourly active-probing signal was 46.0% of its reference median, while the lowest routing signal was 93.4%. Switch measurements, then select a dated utility row to inspect what each source recorded around the same hour.

title: GC Subdomain Watch
description: Compare the official web addresses of Canadian institutions across dated federal directories.

data_info.detail: Archived and current Canada.ca directories supply institutional links. Cert Spotter supplies certificate summaries for four named public homepages.

readme.note: Compare the 2023 and current directory, then filter by destination changes. The two recorded dates bound the change. Each result links to the editions used, and the RSS feed carries observed changes.

title: IX Ledger
description: Compare Canadian internet exchanges across dated snapshots and find which networks appeared, left or changed their listed connections.

data_info.detail: CAIDA’s dated PeeringDB archives record exchange locations, network names and self-reported interface speeds.

readme.note: VANIX had 48 listed ASNs in the November 1, 2018 snapshot and 79 on November 18, 2026. Compare the two editions, then choose Appeared to inspect the individual networks behind the change.

title: Boomerang Meter
description: Compare Canadian anchor pairs and inspect the exchange evidence on their published internet paths.

data_info.detail: Completed RIPE Atlas traces are compared with same-day PeeringDB exchange member addresses and facility countries.

readme.note: On November 18, 2026 all eight completed traces from Beauharnois AS16276 to Vancouver AS396993 matched a DE-CIX New York member interface. The eight reverse traces reached Beauharnois with no exchange match. Compare the directions and open their original Atlas results.

title: Colo Check
description: See which Cloudflare data centre your connection reaches over IPv4 and IPv6, how fast it answers, and whether Canadian traffic crosses the border.

data_info.detail: Your browser reads Cloudflare's /cdn-cgi/trace page from several addresses; data-centre names come from Cloudflare's published location list.

readme.note: Choose "Check my connection". The large code is the data centre your browser's normal route reached. Rows highlighted in orange reached a data centre outside Canada although Cloudflare placed you in Canada. That usually means your ISP hands Cloudflare traffic over in the US (for example, Vancouver traffic served from Seattle). Compare the IPv4 and IPv6 rows: they often take different paths. Save each run with a label such as "Home fibre" or "Phone on 5G", then run it again on another network to compare. Saved runs keep only your network prefix, never your full address.

title: Hosted Where
description: Compare what Canadian institutions disclose about a service provider, mail gateway and storage location.

data_info.detail: Institutional service guides document hosting and storage. Public MX answers for named mail services identify the receiving gateway.

readme.note: Compare Dalhousie email with University of Victoria OneDrive. One guide identifies the mail provider, while the other explicitly locates stored files in Canada. The MX interpreter also accepts records pasted privately.

title: GC Domain Graveyard
description: Recover a Canadian public website from an old name or address and open a dated archival copy.

data_info.detail: Library and Archives Canada identifies historic sites. The Internet Archive supplies additional replay dates for the original URLs.

readme.note: Search for Wheat Board and open a year from the capture timeline. The date belongs to a saved page. The curator’s featured copy and the latest check of the old address have separate labels.

title: Tide & Dark
description: Find photography windows when a modeled Canadian low tide overlaps darkness and a dim Moon.

data_info.detail: TICON-3 coastal gauge constants produce independent low-tide estimates at seven Canadian sites. Solar altitude and lunar illumination are calculated for each station.

readme.note: Try Halifax starting December 1, 2026 with astronomical darkness, at most 25% lunar illumination and one hour on either side of low tide. The December 3 local evening window surrounds a modeled 10:08 p.m. low with a roughly 22% illuminated Moon.

title: Release Receipt
description: See how Canada's monthly GDP growth estimates changed across Statistics Canada releases.

data_info.detail: Statistics Canada’s archived monthly GDP tables show what each release reported for the same month.

dataset.title: Canadian monthly GDP growth as originally published

readme.note: Choose a reference month and an industry group to see the six-month window of growth estimates printed in successive Statistics Canada bulletins. The tool measures the difference between the first regular table and the latest archived table in percentage points. Select a month in the revision ranking to see the dated evidence, or download the figures and their source links.

title: Policy Rate Scorecard
description: Compare market participants’ published rate forecasts with the Bank of Canada’s next decisions.

data_info.detail: Quarterly Bank of Canada survey medians are matched to dated policy decisions and checked weekly.

dataset.title: Bank of Canada survey forecasts and subsequent rate decisions

readme.note: Pick a decision month to see the eligible survey medians, respondent counts and middle halves of responses. Switch to the last public forecast per decision to see how often it matched and the average size of a miss. Download either view as CSV.

title: Export Neighbours
description: Explore where Canadian provinces send lobster, lumber and other domestic exports, and see which destinations gain or lose share.

data_info.detail: Statistics Canada customs records show monthly domestic export value by province of origin, product and destination.

dataset.title: Canadian exports by province, product and destination

readme.note: Choose a province, product and month to see where its domestic exports went. Compare a single month or January through the selected month with the same period one year earlier. Follow one destination’s share across months, inspect the CAD values behind the chart, or download every destination in your comparison. The Nova Scotia preset covers live, fresh or chilled lobster. The British Columbia preset covers five softwood lumber codes.

title: Metro Economy
description: Compare employment and unemployment across Canadian metropolitan areas and see how their labour markets changed.

data_info.detail: Statistics Canada’s Labour Force Survey provides monthly, seasonally adjusted three-month averages for seven labour market indicators.

readme.note: Compare Halifax with Vancouver or Abbotsford–Mission. Pick a month to see how many people were working or looking for work and how their share of the labour force changed. Share the selected comparison or download the underlying monthly estimates.

title: Transit Receipt
description: Save bus arrival predictions and compare them with later vehicle sightings at selected stops.

data_info.detail: Saved Halifax bus arrival estimates are compared with later vehicle sightings; TransLink collection is optional.

readme.note: Start with a Halifax stop, then choose a saved prediction receipt. A positive difference means the first retained vehicle sighting was later than the estimate. A missing sighting stays unmatched; it never becomes an on-time arrival.

title: Tide Receipt
description: Save tomorrow’s tide predictions and compare them with measured water levels at Vancouver and Halifax.

data_info.detail: Canadian Hydrographic Service tide predictions are saved before their target hours and matched to gauge readings.

readme.note: Choose a gauge and a saved receipt. A prediction of 3.2 m followed by a 3.5 m gauge reading gives a −0.3 m signed difference. That residual includes non-tidal effects and is not a storm-surge forecast score.

title: Grid Receipt
description: Track Ontario electricity demand forecasts against subsequently reported hourly demand.

data_info.detail: IESO hourly average demand forecasts are compared with subsequently reported Ontario electricity demand.

readme.note: Select a saved forecast issue. Positive error means the forecast exceeded reported demand. Archived source issues are marked separately from forecasts captured live; both use the same hourly average demand series.

title: Gov Tracker Census
description: Who else does a government homepage contact? Compare observed requests, scripts and cookies across a fixed public website sample.

data_info.detail: Weekly passive browser observations of 15 federal, BC and Nova Scotia homepages.

readme.note: Choose a jurisdiction and open an institution row to inspect its request destinations and cookie names. A third-party request is not proof of tracking. Unavailable scans stay visibly unavailable.

title: Contract Patterns
description: Follow awards, amendments and repeated vendor relationships. Find patterns worth checking against the original disclosures.

data_info.detail: Federal contract disclosures for a rolling year, with reported amendments and award clusters.

readme.note: Set a 7-, 30- or 90-day window and an amount band to find repeated awards to the same normalized vendor within a department. Open a row for reported amendments; these patterns are leads, not findings of contract splitting.

title: Maple Hosting Index
description: A dated sample of .ca domains, observed through DNS. Explore the networks and estimated countries behind their public addresses.

data_info.detail: Monthly DNS, ASN and IP-country observations for 100 .ca domains from a dated Tranco list.

readme.note: Compare the first 100 .ca domains in a dated Tranco ranking. Open a domain for A/AAAA answers, origin ASNs and DB-IP Country Lite country estimates. Multiple networks can serve one domain, so shares may overlap.

title: ATIP Decision Lens
description: Read the published outcomes of access complaints. Compare institutions, issues and findings while keeping the original reports close.

data_info.detail: Published Information Commissioner decisions and final reports, with visible extraction coverage.

readme.note: Filter an institution and Act section, then open a decision for its published finding and original report. Listing/release dates are separate from decision dates. Published decisions are selected reports, not all complaints.

title: ISP Report Card
description: Compare measured internet capabilities, one indicator at a time. See the dates, samples and routing evidence behind each number.

data_info.detail: Separate APNIC IPv6/DNSSEC measurements and RPKI prefix checks for seven Canadian provider ASNs.

readme.note: Compare IPv6 capability, DNSSEC validation and RPKI route authorization separately. Open a provider for dated histories, experiment counts and prefix evidence. There is no composite grade.

title: Donation Radar
description: Explore reported federal contributions and compare return versions. Keep source corrections visible without guessing who a contributor is.

data_info.detail: Submitted and reviewed 2023 registered-party annual contribution records from Elections Canada.

readme.note: Choose a province and submitted or reviewed 2023 annual returns. Ordinary and directed contributions remain separate. A reported name is not a resolved identity; similar names must not be combined as one person.

title: Anycast Compass
description: Which root-server instances do Canadian probes reach? Follow returned instance names and changes in a dated volunteer-probe sample.

data_info.detail: Daily one-hour samples from 50 Canadian RIPE Atlas probes across 13 IPv4 root servers.

readme.note: Filter a root server and probe ASN. Instance names are returned TXT answers, not destinations inferred from IP geography. Province is estimated from obfuscated probe coordinates; volunteer probes are not representative of all ISP customers.

title: Sanctions Ledger
description: Keep a dated record of Canada’s consolidated sanctions entries. Inspect listed identities, regulatory references and changes between captures.

data_info.detail: Dated snapshots and changes in Global Affairs Canada’s consolidated sanctions XML.

readme.note: Open an entry to inspect its identity fields and linked regulation. The diary reports additions, absences and changed source entries between captures. An absence from the consolidated XML is not by itself proof of legal delisting.

title: Border Pulse
description: Canada-bound waits, kept in context. Compare reported crossing conditions, older hourly patterns and monthly service-standard results.

data_info.detail: Canada-bound reports for four BC crossings, with 2019 hourly and later monthly historical data.

readme.note: Choose a crossing and distinguish current reports, the 2019 Q4 hourly sample and newer monthly service-standard percentages. No delay means up to five minutes; missing and conflicting observations are excluded from wait statistics. If a crossing is absent from the current CBSA feed, its historical records remain available and its current report is explicitly unavailable.

title: Order in Council Diary
description: Read the cabinet decisions hiding in plain sight. Search orders, appointments, departments and enabling statutes, then follow what changed.

data_info.detail: A dated index of current-year Orders in Council, with a weekly capture and change feed.

readme.note: Search a department, statute or subject and open the original order. The weekly diary identifies newly observed and changed entries. Approval date is separate from the date the order first appeared in our archive.

title: Maple Phish
description: Canadian-brand phishing signals, with evidence kept in context.

data_info.detail: Daily derived PhishStats summaries and separately labelled URLhaus malware signals; URL-level imports stay in your browser.

readme.note: Choose a brand to inspect derived phishing counts, report-month groups and hosting-ASN groups. Import a PhishStats JSON array or URLhaus response locally to inspect defanged URLs, report dates and supplied registrar data. Brand-token matches are unverified candidates; URLhaus malware is always separate from phishing.

title: Shield Check
description: See which filtering DNS services block fresh phishing and malware domains, including CIRA Canadian Shield, and test your own list.

data_info.detail: Six-hourly captures check fresh URLhaus and OpenPhish domains against CIRA, Cloudflare and Quad9; your own list is checked live from your browser.

readme.note: The scoreboard's block rate counts only domains that still resolved on the operator's unfiltered service, so dead domains don't count against anyone. "Unique" means no other security filter blocked that domain in the same capture. A control-list block is a false positive worth reporting to the provider. "How quickly" tracks domains that first appear in a feed after tracking began and shows how many hours passed before each filter blocked them. Use "Check your own list" to test a suspicious link before you share it. That check runs from your browser, and services that don't accept browser requests show "!".

title: Scan Receipt
description: Inspect dated website screenshots and network requests, and compare saved receipts.

data_info.detail: Daily browser captures, owner-selected public receipts and urlscan workflows for twelve owned sites; provider imports stay local.

readme.note: Start with a saved CoolCode receipt, choose Inspect receipt to see its screenshot and network responses, then compare two captures of the same page. Daily first-party captures establish a baseline and build history. The owner-only urlscan workflow accepts configured owned pages and returns provider links; its output is separate from the public browser-capture archive. Use Receipts · Capture and publish with capture_url to add a permanent public browser receipt. Visitors can also import public urlscan Result JSON locally; download receipts to keep local imports.

title: Gov Grade
description: Compare dated security assessments and locally imported reports.

data_info.detail: Dated MDN header reports for twelve owned sites, local comparisons and personal SSL Labs checks; government rows are coverage notes.

readme.note: Inspect the saved CoolCode header report and individual MDN findings. The owner can run Personal TLS · Check an owned site in GitHub Actions selecting any configured owned hostname and using SSLLABS_EMAIL, then open the provider report from the run Summary. Existing MDN JSON imports stay in this tab for comparison. The HTTP grade explanation lists provider point deductions and keeps it distinct from TLS. Available reports are shown first; uncollected government targets appear only when explicitly viewing coverage notes.

title: Rack Expiry
description: Match your software inventory to published support windows and plan the next upgrade.

data_info.detail: Saved endoflife.date support windows are matched to a private inventory in your browser.

readme.note: Add an asset label, software product and installed version. Rack Expiry matches the longest numeric release cycle from a saved endoflife.date catalogue, then sorts support-ended and upcoming deadlines first. Choose an assessment date, inspect the release reference, and export results as CSV. Imports accept simple three-column CSV (asset,product,version) or a JSON array; exported CSV files include evidence columns and can be imported again using their named inventory fields. CSV prefixes formula-leading cells for spreadsheet safety, which can alter labels on reimport; choose **Save inventory JSON** for a lossless backup and exact roundtrip. Inventory stays in memory until **Save on this device**; only that explicit action writes namespaced local storage. No inventory fields are uploaded. The example stack is illustrative. Standard upstream support, active support and extended support differ: purchased entitlements and distribution backports must be checked separately. Unknown versions stay unknown. Numeric prefix matching requires an entirely numeric installed version; nonnumeric release-cycle names match exactly, ignoring case. Prerelease or malformed suffixes are not treated as stable releases. A support deadline is not proof of an exploitable vulnerability. Upstream deadline dates are the last supported day (the status changes the following day). Boolean-only statuses with no known end date are used only on the catalogue check date, so historical or future assessments remain unknown instead of inventing coverage. The API’s `isMaintained` flag can include extended support and is not used to infer standard support. The selected product catalogue refreshes Mondays at 10:43 UTC. Changed catalogues are retained as immutable compressed JSON archives with hashes, dates and a change feed; a first capture is a baseline, not retroactive history. The public app works from the last validated saved snapshot. No API key is needed.

title: Mushroom Calendar
description: Explore when local fungi were observed around Langley and Halifax, with seasonal patterns, quality filters and a privacy-conscious map.

data_info.detail: Public iNaturalist fungi observations from 2023–2025 in fixed Langley and Halifax areas, rechecked weekly with retained captures.

readme.note: Start with research-grade observations, compare the monthly share on each coast, then select a month or taxon to inspect its records. The 2023–2025 calendar describes observation activity, not abundance, edibility or a forecast; obscured records have month-only dates and never appear on the map.

title: Law Delta
description: Search BC legislation titles and compare section-level changes across captured privacy laws.

data_info.detail: Weekly BC Laws title catalogue plus immutable CiviX XML captures of four privacy laws. Broader title search does not imply full-text history for all laws.

readme.note: Search the wider BC legislation title catalogue and full text across the four privacy laws in the selected capture. Historical versions and legislative change tables are labelled separately. Open a section to inspect its recorded text and compare captures. Observation dates are distinct from effective dates; catalogue title matches do not add change history for other laws.

title: Dawn Chorus
description: Listen to the same bird species across Atlantic and Pacific Canada, with recording-level provenance.

data_info.detail: Weekly xeno-canto API v3 snapshots of six bird species in British Columbia and Atlantic Canada, with original audio and recording-level licences.

readme.note: Choose a species to compare original xeno-canto recordings from British Columbia and Atlantic Canada. Filter by sound, recording month or quality, switch between source recordings, and export attributed metadata. Six focal species and the first 100 records per species/province query form a bounded sample; different individuals, dates, equipment and habitats mean these examples do not establish regional dialects. Cards show recording dates separately from upload dates, plus recordist, source and individual licence. The initial page honestly shows a pending state until its first authenticated collection; a previously saved Dawn Chorus JSON snapshot can also be opened locally.

title: Radar Scope
description: Read Canadian internet traffic and disruption signals through Cloudflare Radar observations.

data_info.detail: Daily Cloudflare Radar captures of hourly HTTP traffic and IP shares, with Canadian outage annotations and retained history.

readme.note: Inspect seven days of hourly Canadian HTTP traffic and compare its daily rhythm with the United States or United Kingdom. Each country is normalized independently to its own maximum (0–1), so the curves compare shape, not traffic volume or market share. IPv4/IPv6 percentages describe the observed HTTP request mix. Canadian outage annotations cover a separate 30-day source window and are not an exhaustive outage register. Choose a retained capture, inspect gaps and source dates, or open/export a local snapshot without an API key in your browser.

title: Museum Drawer
description: Open a local cabinet of historic specimens and modern biodiversity records around Langley and Halifax.

data_info.detail: Dated GBIF samples compare historic preserved specimens with modern biodiversity records around Langley and Halifax; source totals, licences and sampling limits stay visible.

readme.note: Choose Langley or Halifax, then compare historic preserved specimens (1700–1999) with modern records (2000 onward). Up to 300 records per time band are retained; these capped API-order samples are not representative surveys. Filter by taxon, source, licence or coordinate quality, inspect an attributed record card, and export the selection. The coarse map and decade chart show only the selected capture’s retained records, not every GBIF match or a population trend.

title: Hotspot Ledger
description: Compare recent bird reports from Iona Beach and Hartlen Point, with a clear view of shared species and notable sightings.

data_info.detail: A daily derived eBird API comparison of the latest reports at Iona Beach and Hartlen Point within 30 days; not historical totals.

readme.note: Compare the latest accepted report for each species at the two exact hotspots, then filter to shared species, one coast's feed, or eBird notable species. The full 30-day view preserves every report returned by eBird's rolling source window; shorter windows are anchored to that capture date. Species counts are recent-feed counts, not seasonal or historical totals. Missing reports do not establish absence, and observer effort differs. Download the filtered derived CSV or a JSON snapshot; reopening either file happens only in the browser tab.

title: API Archaeology
description: Inspect published API definitions, compare operations and schemas, and follow dated specification captures.

data_info.detail: Weekly retained APIs.guru definitions, with optional local OpenAPI JSON comparison.

readme.note: API Archaeology watches six public API definitions in the APIs.guru directory: Apicurio Registry, Canada Holidays, APIs.guru itself, NASA APOD, NASA Asteroids and Wikimedia. Select an API, then a “from” and “to” definition. Each choice includes the version and actual collection date. The first capture includes two genuine Apicurio versions, so a meaningful comparison is available immediately; other single-version APIs start as inventories until another collection is retained. Search by method, path, summary or change type. Select an operation for authentication, parameters, response codes and field-level evidence. The shared-schema inventory provides a second view of additions, removals and changed definitions. “Changed” means the specification differs; it is not a compatibility judgment or proof that a live service behaves differently. Directory update dates can be old and are not provider release dates. You can also select two local OpenAPI 3.x or Swagger 2.0 JSON files (10 MB each); omit the first file to inspect an inventory. These files stay in the current browser tab and are not uploaded or saved. YAML is not supported. Export JSON for the complete compared evidence and source hashes, or CSV for the operation inventory. Collection runs weekly on Tuesday at 07:13 UTC through GitHub Actions, subject to scheduler delays. The workflow can also be run manually with “Capture fresh public definitions before building” enabled. All definitions must validate and all checks must pass before new data is committed and the site is deployed. Earlier captures remain available. No keys or API registrations are needed: the collector reads specification documents only and never invokes the APIs they describe.

title: Government Data Gap Detector
description: Follow changes, publication gaps and download availability in a curated federal dataset watchlist.

data_info.detail: Weekly observations of eight federal CKAN records retain metadata changes and sampled resource responses; network errors are not treated as deleted data.

readme.note: Choose a dataset to inspect its declared update frequency, metadata dates and sampled download responses. Set an optional metadata-age threshold for your own review, then save an evidence note with source links and timestamps. The first capture is a baseline: a blocked request does not mean a missing file, and an old metadata date does not prove the underlying data is overdue.

title: Research Ledger
description: Search research metadata, inspect funding and updates, and follow dated Crossref records.

data_info.detail: Crossref bibliographic metadata from live searches and weekly snapshots of three Canadian topic queries; selected records, not complete research coverage.

readme.note: Start with the saved wildfire, water or open-government collection, then inspect a paper's authors, funding and recorded update links. Search Crossref by topic, title, author or DOI for other work; export a CSV or save a timestamped receipt. Missing funding or correction metadata means unknown, and citation counts are incomplete—not a measure of quality.

title: Status Ledger
description: Keep a dated record of official cloud-service incidents, maintenance and changes.

data_info.detail: Official GitHub and DigitalOcean status APIs supply daily incident, maintenance and component captures, with up to 90 retained collections.

readme.note: Choose a provider, component, incident or maintenance state, or event date range, then inspect a report’s original update timeline. The two provider cards show the different feed windows; their incident counts are not a reliability ranking. Choose two retained captures to find newly observed records, changed text and records no longer present. The first capture establishes a baseline: earlier dates in an incident timeline are provider-supplied history, not earlier CoolCode captures. Download a filtered CSV or the complete selected capture JSON. Daily collection keeps the latest 90 successful captures; disappearance from a feed never implies resolution.

title: Query Plan Lab
description: Read MySQL and MariaDB execution plans, inspect table access and compare optimizer estimates before and after a change.

data_info.detail: MySQL and MariaDB EXPLAIN JSON plans are parsed and compared locally in your browser.

readme.note: Paste a MySQL or MariaDB JSON execution plan, or open a local JSON file, then choose **Visualize plan**. Add a second plan to compare access types, chosen indexes, row estimates, filtering and reported cost. Select any tree node to inspect the source JSON and any available MariaDB `r_rows` / `r_loops` measurements. The built-in comparison is an explicitly hand-written illustration, not a benchmark. Plans stay in memory in your browser; JSON and CSV downloads are optional. No account, API key or database connection is needed. Supports the traditional `query_block` JSON layout, including EXPLAIN-column exports; text/TREE output and MySQL JSON format version 2 are not supported.

title: Filing Delta
description: Compare reported financial periods and trace changed values back to SEC filings.

data_info.detail: Dated SEC EDGAR filings and selected financial facts from a configurable company watchlist; refreshed daily.

readme.note: Choose a company from the watchlist, then select a financial concept, currency and period basis. The ledger compares exact reported periods and links each value to its SEC filing; a changed value may reflect a recast or context difference, not necessarily a restatement. Daily captures retain selected standard financial facts from 2018 onward, not a complete company or filing universe.

title: FX Receipt
description: Compare a foreign-currency purchase with a dated reference rate and save an inspectable conversion receipt.

data_info.detail: Frankfurter historical reference rates with transaction calculations kept in your browser.

readme.note: Enter your purchase and final posted charge, then compare with a dated reference. A positive difference is above that benchmark; it does not prove the difference was a separately charged fee. Save JSON to retain the exact rate and reopen the receipt later.

title: Package Pulse
description: Inspect npm release histories, maintainers and dependencies, then compare packages with dated CDN usage.

data_info.detail: Live public npm metadata and jsDelivr CDN usage, with dated default captures for immediate exploration.

readme.note: Enter any public npm package, optionally add a second, and choose Look up live. The latest publisher tag can differ from the newest release; CDN requests are not npm downloads or unique users.

title: Art Timeline
description: Explore two museum collections through time and compare artworks, materials and original records.

data_info.detail: Search The Met and Art Institute of Chicago, with a dated opening collection and public-domain images.

readme.note: Search either museum with your own terms, then refine the loaded works and compare two objects with their original date labels and credits. The opening collection and search presets are editable in web/config.json; they do not limit live searches.

title: Label Compare
description: Compare food labels by barcode: nutrition, ingredients, allergens and missing information side by side.

data_info.detail: Live Open Food Facts barcode lookups, dated starter labels and local receipt comparisons.

readme.note: Enter any food barcode to compare nutrition, including reported vitamins and minerals, ingredients and allergens. Inspect original label photos and additional product details. Switch between source-normalized 100 g/mL and each product’s own serving, then save a dated JSON receipt to reopen later; missing fields never become zero or an allergy-free claim.

title: Headline Vault
description: Search historic newspaper pages and export a source-linked research trail.

data_info.detail: Live Library of Congress searches plus dated, configurable starting-search captures.

readme.note: Search any topic with dates, publication place or a newspaper LCCN; pin useful pages and save a JSON receipt or CSV. Saved starting searches load instantly; live searches query the Library of Congress. If a browser cannot read its response, open the exact source JSON and import it locally with its search URL. OCR matches and newspaper claims need checking against the original page.

title: Old News Oddities
description: Follow curious historical newspaper reports, search your own phrases and save a trail of original pages.

data_info.detail: Editable discovery shelves and live full-text page searches from Library of Congress Chronicling America.

readme.note: Choose a topic or search your own phrase, then open the original page to check the OCR and surrounding columns. Topic matches are historical reports, not verified events; save useful pages and export their source links. If a live request fails, import an official Library JSON response with its exact search URL; clippings stay usable and imports are clearly dated as imports.

title: Marine Names
description: Resolve marine scientific names, inspect their taxonomy and follow reported distributions and sources.

data_info.detail: Look up WoRMS scientific names live or inspect dated coastal reference records.

readme.note: Search any scientific name or AphiaID; enable prefix matching to explore a genus and load additional pages. Four dated coastal examples open immediately, and are starting points rather than a search restriction. The record distinguishes accepted names from synonyms and alternative representations. It shows the source’s modification date separately from the retrieval date; synonyms are current relationships, not a historical change timeline. Distribution records are incomplete and do not establish present-day occurrence. Download the selected record as JSON or its name fields as CSV; import an earlier JSON export locally. Expand saved coverage in `web/config.json`, run `python3 scripts/refresh.py`, then commit the new capture, manifest and configuration. No registration or API key is required.

title: Civic Lookup
description: Find Canadian representatives and electoral districts by postal code or coordinates, with source links and downloadable lookup receipts.

data_info.detail: Search Represent by Open North by postal code or coordinates, with a dated public-place example and downloadable lookup receipts.

readme.note: Civic Lookup accepts **any syntactically valid Canadian postal code**, or latitude/longitude entered explicitly. Search is not restricted to the city presets. It shows source-reported representative names, offices, districts, assemblies, parties and public office contacts, with official profile/source links. Filter by government level or text, inspect boundary records, and save CSV or a complete JSON lookup receipt. JSON receipts can be reopened locally without sending them to a provider. The opening Ottawa city-centre result is a dated, real saved example, not a live lookup. A submitted lookup sends only the chosen coordinates or postal code (plus normal connection information) to Open North. There is no automatic geolocation or local search history. Receipts include the location query: review them before sharing. Postal codes can overlap districts. Available **centroid** and **concordance** matches are combined, deduplicated and labelled. Open North omits representative groups with no matches; these are accepted as empty groups while the original response is preserved in exported receipts. Coordinates narrow the geographic match, but neither method guarantees current officeholders or complete municipal coverage. A retrieval date is not an election date or source-update date. Other boundary records may include historical district versions, school boards and statistical areas; records linked to a returned representative are labelled separately. Confirm contacts and electoral eligibility through the official institution or election authority. **Expand or customize:** edit `web/config.json`. Change `defaultQuery`, add/remove `presets` (any postal code or coordinates), or tune `pageSize`, `maxPages`, `timeoutMs`, `requestGapMs` and `importMaxBytes`. Presets only fill the form; pressing **Find representatives** submits it. No allowlist of places exists. To replace the saved public example, set `defaultQuery` to a public location and run `python3 scripts/refresh_example.py`, then commit `web/config.json` and `web/data/example.json`. The collector preserves the last-good file on an error and rejects truncated examples. Run the repository's **Browser tool · Check and publish** workflow after committing; main-branch changes build and publish automatically. There is no scheduled collector and no need to rerun it to search a new location.

title: Stream Atlas
description: Find internet radio across countries, languages and genres, then build your own listening collection.

data_info.detail: Radio Browser supplies station metadata, with a dated starting collection and live directory searches.

readme.note: Search beyond the starting shelf by station name, country, language or genre; the presets are shortcuts, not a fixed list. Playing connects directly to a station, while saved stations remain in the current tab unless you opt into device storage or export a copy.

title: Password Exposure Check
description: Check whether a password appears in known breach data, without sending the password or its full hash.

data_info.detail: Pwned Passwords supplies matching hash ranges; the password and full comparison stay in your browser.

readme.note: Enter a password and explicitly choose **Check exposure**. Only the first five SHA-1 hash characters go to Pwned Passwords; the browser compares the returned range locally and clears the input after a successful check. A missing match does not prove the password is safe, and a match does not identify an account or a particular breach. Clear everything removes this tab's input and result.

title: Book Graveyard
description: Find old books, compare their editions, and follow the trail to a readable copy.

data_info.detail: Searches Open Library book and edition metadata, with a dated opening selection and reading links.

readme.note: Search any title, author, subject or set of words, optionally limiting the work's first-publication years and Open Library's access category. The starting searches are editable suggestions, not a fixed collection. Results are paginated. Open **Compare editions** on a work, then choose two publication records to compare publisher, date, language, pages, format and ISBN. A work groups editions; its first-publication year and reading-access label do not describe every edition. The opening screen uses a small, dated real Open Library capture. **Search books** retrieves live results directly from Open Library; failures preserve the previous results. Add books to a reading shelf, export JSON/CSV, or import a saved search/shelf JSON locally. The shelf stays in the current tab unless **Remember this shelf on this device** is selected. A readable-copy label is not a worldwide public-domain determination, and borrowing can require an Open Library/Internet Archive account. “Graveyard” is a discovery theme, not a claim that titles are forgotten or out of print. **Expand or customize:** edit `web/config.json` to change `defaultSearch`, add any number of `presets`, or change page sizes and timeouts. Each query has `query`, `field` (`all`, `title`, `author`, `subject`), `from`, `to`, `access` (`any`, `public`, `borrowable`, `no_ebook`) and `sort` (`relevance`, `old`, `new`). Visitors can type searches beyond these presets. After changing the opening search, run `python3 scripts/refresh_data.py` once; review `web/data/opening.json`, then run the normal checks and commit to `main`. The Pages workflow builds and publishes the change. This tool needs no API key; Open Library asks the owner to register the application/use case using the form linked in its API documentation.

title: Format Shift
description: Trace an album through vinyl, tape, disc and digital editions with MusicBrainz metadata.

data_info.detail: MusicBrainz release metadata, with a retained edition selection and on-demand artist and release searches.

readme.note: Search any artist name, choose the matching MusicBrainz artist, and load additional pages as needed. You can also paste a **release** or **release-group** UUID or MusicBrainz link. A release is one edition; a release group joins editions of the same album. Format filters, date filters, a decade chart and two-edition comparison work on the records loaded into the page. Counts describe recorded editions, not sales, popularity, availability or the entire music industry. The opening view contains eight real selected Rush *Moving Pictures* editions, with capture time and source links. They are selected records rather than a complete discography. Fetch all album editions or search another artist to expand. **Save receipt** exports the current collection; **Import receipt** opens that JSON locally; **Export visible CSV** exports the filtered view. Imported files never leave the browser. Source failures preserve the current collection. The owner can also run the **Music metadata · Collect a receipt** workflow for any artist, release group or release UUID, then import its downloadable JSON. **Expand or customize:** edit `web/config.json`: `presets` changes example artists, `opening.releaseIds` changes retained editions, `opening.title` and `opening.releaseGroupId` describe that selection, and `pageSize` / `maxLoadedReleases` control browsing. Commit an edit to `web/config.json` on `main` and the Pages workflow automatically fetches the configured opening editions, records a successful API receipt in `web/data/opening.json`, and publishes it. A source failure keeps the last good receipt. You can also run `python3 scripts/collect.py` locally, review the JSON and commit it. New entries require no UI source changes. `apiBase` can point to the optional identified server adapter documented below. No MusicBrainz account or API key is needed for public reads; the hosted API's free use is for noncommercial applications.

title: Malware Lineage
description: Follow dated malware metadata, reported URL-to-hash connections and changing provider observations.

data_info.detail: Selected dated URLhaus and MalwareBazaar metadata; daily authenticated collection, local receipt imports.

readme.note: Browse captured URL and file metadata, search a hash, family, tag or defanged URL, and select a record for its source observations. Choose a second dated capture to compare changed fields. Save receipts as JSON or export the filtered rows as CSV. Import a saved receipt to inspect it locally. To expand the daily collection, edit `web/config.json`; the page creates a valid watch entry for you. Run **Malware Lineage · Collect, check and publish** in GitHub Actions for a one-time hash, URLhaus ID, tag or family lookup. The API key stays in GitHub. A missing record in a later selected sample does not mean it was removed from the provider or that a URL was cleaned.

title: Launch Ledger
description: Keep a dated record of launch schedules, compare changes and follow provider-reported outcomes.

data_info.detail: Daily Launch Library 2 captures retain announced launch times, precision and reported status for a configurable date window and watchlist.

readme.note: Choose a capture and an earlier comparison, then select a launch to see changes to its reported time, precision, status and pad. History begins with the first collection; a passed NET date does not prove liftoff. Edit web/config.json to expand the date window or add launch UUIDs to watchIds, then push to main to refresh automatically. Downloads keep your own copy; imported receipts stay in the current tab.

title: Plate Solve Lab
description: Turn an Astrometry.net solve into a dated sky-position receipt. Inspect field size, orientation and identified objects; compare two photographs.

data_info.detail: Dated Astrometry.net metadata, imported receipts and owner-triggered image solves; photos are submitted only by an explicit action.

readme.note: Open **Open real example** to explore a genuine Leo Triplet solve. Use **Import receipt JSON** to load one or more receipts; **Save receipts JSON** downloads your session. Receipts stay only in the tab until saved. Comparison reports centre separation, orientation change and pixel-scale change. To solve your own image, follow the owner upload link to https://platesolve-api.hackme.ca/, which opens in a separate tab. Sign in as the allowed owner, choose a local JPEG, PNG or FITS sky photo (up to 10 MB), confirm your permission to send it to Astrometry.net, then upload and solve. Download the completed JSON receipt, return to Plate Solve Lab and choose **Import receipt JSON**. If solving is still queued, keep the submission ID and use **Check submission** in the portal later. The portal also reads existing Astrometry job IDs. The public viewer stays open to everyone; the linked upload portal requires the owner's Access sign-in. The **Owner solve workflow** remains an alternative for public HTTPS image URLs and existing jobs. Choose **Run workflow**, supply exactly one input, then download the **plate-solve-receipt** artifact, unzip it and import `receipt.json`. Use **submission_id** to resume a queued submission without uploading again. The repository secret `ASTROMETRY_API_KEY` is used only by Actions; the portal has its own Worker Secret. The public page never asks for your API key. Its owner link is configurable through `web/config.json` → `ownerPortalUrl`; this simply opens the protected page. The separate `adapterUrl` setting remains empty because inline cross-origin upload is not enabled. Visitors can also upload through Astrometry.net using their own account and inspect its native results. The real example works immediately with no service setup.

title: Road Pulse
description: Follow BC road incidents, construction and reopening estimates through dated DriveBC captures.

data_info.detail: Dated DriveBC Open511 events, collected every six hours. Compare event IDs, source schedules and timing notes without treating disappearance as reopening.

readme.note: Search any road, town or event ID in the captured BC feed, choose an area/severity/type, and explore the matching events on the interactive map. Lines retain the source's reported road geometry; dots show source points. Click either a map feature or a list entry to select the same event receipt. **Fit results** frames every mapped result, **Zoom to selected** focuses one event, and **Show on this map** returns from a receipt to its location. The keyboard-accessible event list stays available, including records without usable coordinates. The initial capture contains real DriveBC records; history grows after subsequent successful collections. The source's **ACTIVE** status includes future planned work. **ARCHIVED** does not necessarily mean reopened. An absent event is labelled **no longer in capture**, never reopened. The map and list follow the same dated capture and filters. Grey dashed geometry represents an absent event's last known position; it does not mean the road reopened. Hide the map at any time. Background tiles load only while the map is visible; a tile-service failure leaves road geometry and receipts usable. Choose a dated capture and an earlier one to compare description, road state, schedule and other source fields by event ID. Timing notes quote relevant sentences from the source; no reopening date is invented. Open **Load last … captures** for an event's recent observation history. The observed timestamp and the source's last-update timestamp are separate. Schedule end times are planned, not verified actual outcomes. Use **Save capture JSON** for a portable receipt, **Export results CSV** for the filtered list, and **Import capture** to inspect a prior download locally. Imports are not uploaded or persisted. Saved filter views use only this browser's local storage. **Check latest saved capture** reloads published data; **Collect now** opens the GitHub workflow for the owner to run a fresh collection. Consult DriveBC for live travel decisions.

title: River Pulse
description: Follow Canadian river gauges, compare seasonal water levels and discharge, and retain dated source receipts.

data_info.detail: Search ECCC's station catalogue, explore retained Canadian gauge observations, or fetch recent readings and historical daily means for any station.

readme.note: River Pulse starts with real captures for the Nicomekl River in Langley, the Fraser River at Hope and the Sackville River at Bedford. Search a station name or ECCC number, choose recent days and two comparison years, then select **Fetch this station**. For a closed gauge or empty period, select **Find archive dates**, then **Use available years** and **Fetch this station**. This checks actual measured records, so a historical gauge does not leave you guessing which years to try. Switch between discharge (m³/s) and water level (metres at that gauge's datum). Recent unit observations and historical daily means have separate charts; gaps stay empty. Save a JSON receipt to reopen later, export the station's observations as CSV, or import a receipt into the current tab. Dated published captures can be compared for changed values and qualifiers at overlapping observation times. A first capture establishes a record; it does not invent earlier history. Use the linked official station for source context. Water levels are not comparable flood-risk scores across stations. To expand the automatically collected stations, edit `stationIds` and `defaultStation` in `web/config.json`; no code or API key is needed. Change `historicalYears` and `realtimeDays` there as well. The refresh workflow runs daily, manually, and after configuration/collector changes on main. Every successful capture is retained. A failed refresh preserves the previous public data.

title: Access Receipt
description: Inspect dated accessibility findings, compare changes and keep the evidence.

data_info.detail: Weekly axe-core checks of configured public pages, with local import of your own axe reports.

readme.note: Start with the latest published capture or import a standard axe-core JSON report. The summary counts individual flagged element locations and distinct rule types: one repeated component can produce many locations. The separate review count means human judgement is needed, not that those checks failed. Select an earlier capture and open **Changes** to see newly observed and no-longer-observed rule/element pairs. Comparisons require the same URL, final URL, axe version, browser, viewport, rule tags and settle time. A failed, missing or incomplete-resource page is unassessed. Raw axe imports without the full capture profile can be inspected but cannot establish changes. **Needs review** is separate from confirmed automated findings. There is no accessibility grade or conformance certificate. To expand the collection, edit the `pages` array in `web/config.json`, or run the GitHub workflow with comma-separated public URLs you are authorized to check. Imports stay in this tab; download a receipt to keep it.

title: Dock Diary
description: Find bike-share stations and compare how often bikes or return spaces were unavailable.

data_info.detail: CityBikes station availability with retained hourly captures and optional current network lookups.

readme.note: Choose a network and use **Fetch current availability**, then select a station to inspect bikes, return spaces and a weekday/hour heatmap. Vancouver starts with a real retained capture; the history grows through hourly scheduled checks. An empty heatmap cell means no observations, not uninterrupted availability. A percentage is the share of sampled, distinct observations with zero bikes or spaces, not the share of time unavailable and not a trip count. Download **Save diary JSON** before closing the tab to retain manual lookups; imports and comparisons stay local. Edit **web/config.json** to add tracked networks and their time zones, then run **Dock Diary · Capture, check and publish** to begin retaining them.

title: Buoy Bench
description: Compare Canadian buoy observations and retained marine forecasts across time.

data_info.detail: ECCC buoy observations and marine forecast editions, retained with separate observation, issue and capture times.

readme.note: Choose a buoy, comparison buoy and dated capture. Wind is shown in knots, significant wave height in metres, and water temperature in °C; each plotted point is a source observation. Select a retained forecast edition to read what ECCC issued and inspect the later observations. Forecasts describe areas while buoys measure points, so this is a manual comparison rather than an accuracy score. First-run forecasts correctly show that later observations are still awaited. Save a receipt JSON to keep the record outside this tab.

title: Orbital Census
description: Explore the satellite catalogue by launch, owner and object type, and compare dated captures.

data_info.detail: Dated CelesTrak SATCAT records with source edition times, object fields and capture comparisons.

readme.note: Search **RADARSAT**, **25544**, or an international designator; filters cover the complete retained catalogue, including payloads, rocket bodies and debris. **Canadian objects** is a starting search, not the only supported owner. Select an object for source fields and its CelesTrak record. A blank decay date does not establish that an object is still in Earth orbit. **Dated captures** compares matching coverage across source editions; the first capture establishes a baseline. Save capture JSON or export the filtered CSV to keep evidence, and import saved JSON or JSON.gz captures locally. Default comparisons cover identity and status; orbital measurements are optional and can vary without proving a manoeuvre.

title: Flight Weather
description: Keep airport forecasts and compare them with later observations.

data_info.detail: Retained NOAA/NWS airport forecasts and observations, with issue, validity and capture times.

readme.note: Choose an airport and a dated capture, then select a TAF edition. **Saved before observation** shows only outcomes that occurred after this tool had saved that forecast. A new collection can have no such outcomes yet; hourly captures grow the record. **Issued before observation (reconstructed)** can inspect earlier observations but is explicitly labelled retrospective. TEMPO and PROB alternatives stay separate, and BECMG transitions are excluded from deterministic pairing until the next FM period. Save receipt JSON to keep a portable copy.

title: Ephemera Atlas
description: Search historical menus, postcards and pamphlets by date, place and subject, then inspect original scans.

data_info.detail: Selected NYPL public-domain metadata from its 30 December 2015 archive; searched locally.

readme.note: Search a word such as **railroad** or use **Canadian traces** to find mentions in titles, subjects and notes. The separate place filter searches only recorded geographic subjects and publication places, which many items lack. Open a title for its original dates, source notes, rights and NYPL scan link. **Compare** keeps two records side by side; **Save record JSON** downloads the evidence. Optional scan previews contact NYPL; all searches stay in this tab. This is a selected edition of NYPL’s **30 December 2015** public-domain metadata release, not a live search or a complete inventory of its collections. The download date is separate from the original item date. Year filters overlap recorded ranges; the chart counts each item by its earliest recorded year. Missing dates remain explicitly undated.

title: Fireball Ledger
description: Explore reported fireballs, compare their energies and retain changes to the published catalogue.

data_info.detail: Weekly captures of the NASA/JPL CNEOS catalogue preserve reported fireball locations, energies and subsequent catalogue changes.

readme.note: Start with **At least 1 kt**, then select a map point or an event time in the table to inspect its source values. Change the dates or energy threshold freely; the presets are optional. Events without reported coordinates remain in the ledger but are omitted from the map. **Save capture JSON** keeps the entire selected capture and its changes; **Export filtered CSV** saves only the current results. The capture date is when the catalogue was retrieved, not when the fireball occurred. The first capture is a baseline; later weekly captures show revisions to same-time records and records newly appearing or no longer present. A changed event time can appear as both an addition and an absence because the source provides no immutable event identifier.

title: Charge Gaps
description: Explore charging locations and find where recorded coverage thins out.

data_info.detail: Dated Open Charge Map country exports, searched locally with straight-line distances and provider attribution.

readme.note: Start with **Langley**, select a connector and minimum power, then compare the nearest matching record and the number inside your radius. Enter any valid coordinates to investigate another point; the shortcuts are optional. Distances are straight lines, not driving routes, and an empty result means no matching record in this capture—not proof that no charger exists. **Recorded access** and **Recorded status** include private, restricted and planned locations unless filtered. The source export date is prominent because these downloads can be much older than their retrieval date. Save capture JSON to keep a portable record; imports and coordinate calculations stay in this tab.

title: RFC Trail
description: Follow Internet specifications through their updates, replacements and publication history.

data_info.detail: The full RFC Editor metadata index, retained weekly for local search and relationship comparisons.

readme.note: Search **9110** for HTTP Semantics, **DNS** for a topic, or an author's name. Select an RFC, then follow **Obsoletes**, **Obsoleted by**, **Updates** and **Updated by**. The timeline is ordered by publication month, not by the date a status changed. Extend the trail to two or three connections to inspect a wider family. RFC status and replacement are separate facts: an obsolete document is not automatically Historic, and not every RFC is a standard. Save trail JSON or export filtered CSV to retain the evidence. A first capture establishes the baseline; later changed index captures enable comparisons.

title: Commons Lens
description: Find openly licensed images and audio, inspect rights and build a source-linked attribution.

data_info.detail: Search Wikimedia Commons on demand and retain each work’s creator, original record and reported licence.

readme.note: Search **Halifax waterfront**, then open **Inspect & credit** on a work to find its original record and reported licence. Licence and creator filters narrow the returned page, not the whole catalogue; inspect later pages or loosen a filter if a page has no matches. **Shortlist** keeps selections only in this tab. Save receipt JSON before closing; an imported receipt is processed locally. Always verify the original record before reusing a work.

title: Magnetic North
description: Calculate magnetic declination and convert bearings using the World Magnetic Model.

data_info.detail: NOAA/BGS WMM2025 coefficients calculate the magnetic field locally for dates in 2025–2029.

readme.note: Enter latitude, longitude, WGS84 ellipsoid height and a date in **2025–2029**, or start with Langley or Halifax. East declination is positive: **true bearing = magnetic bearing + declination**. The compass drawing is a schematic, not a reading from your device. The chart shows one model’s predictions at a fixed place, not observed magnetic history. Save receipt JSON or CSV to retain your result; inputs are not saved automatically. Add places in **web/config.json** and push to publish them.

title: Restroom Reach
description: Find mapped toilets, inspect accessibility details and keep a dated local record.

data_info.detail: Dated OpenStreetMap toilet extracts with reported access and accessibility tags; map details can be incomplete or old.

readme.note: Choose a region, then filter wheelchair access, fees or changing tables. **Mapped yes** is a contributor’s report; **Not recorded** is a separate state. Expand **Sort by distance from a point** for coordinates or the Willoughby, Vancouver and Halifax presets. Distances are straight-line, not walking routes. Turn on **Show street map** only when you want background tiles. The capture date and OSM database edition are displayed separately: downloading an old source edition does not make the observations current. Export a receipt to retain the evidence outside this tab. A refresh collects all configured regions before publishing; a failed or incomplete region keeps the last good capture available.

title: Translation Desk
description: Translate text on your device or your own server, then review and export paired passages.

data_info.detail: On-device browser translation or a LibreTranslate server you choose, with local paragraph review and exports.

readme.note: Choose source and target language codes, prepare the browser language pair, then select **Translate**. Preparation may download a language pack; it does not upload your source text. The original and editable translation are paired by paragraph order, so review their alignment and wording. If this browser lacks the Translator API, use your LibreTranslate server or paste an existing translation for local review. **Save project** keeps the texts and glossary; nothing is saved automatically and server keys are excluded.

title: Diagram Bench
description: Turn diagram text into clear, editable SVG and PNG diagrams in your browser.

data_info.detail: Mermaid renders locally; optional Kroki rendering sends code only to a server you choose.

readme.note: Choose a starting point or write your own Mermaid source, then select **Render diagram**. The preview and exported image keep the last successful render when a later edit has a syntax error. **Save project** includes that rendered source so it can be reopened and edited. Mermaid runs locally; selecting Kroki requires your own server address and an explicit permission checkbox before code is sent there.

title: Word Weave
description: Find related words and explore local text statistics, Unicode, cleanup and transformations.

data_info.detail: Datamuse word searches run on demand; text statistics, Unicode inspection and transformations run locally.

readme.note: Start with **ocean** and **Similar meaning**, then pin the search and try **river** to inspect shared words. **Spelling pattern** accepts * for any letters and ? for one letter, such as **t??k**. Syllable and word-class filters are local, so they make no additional API request. Comparisons describe only the returned lists, not the entire vocabulary. Your shortlist stays in this tab; download it before closing. Switch to **Text utilities** for word counts and frequency, spacing cleanup, case/slug conversion and Unicode inspection. Transformations preview beside the original; choose **Use output as original** only when you want to replace it.

title: Holiday Clock
description: Compare holiday calendars and count working days with rules you can inspect.

data_info.detail: Canada Holidays records and local date-holidays rules compare calendars; custom working-day assumptions stay in your browser.

readme.note: Compare any supported countries and first-level regions, with British Columbia and Nova Scotia as the starting pair. Canada can use nominal or observed dates; other calendars retain their own substitute rules. Export a comparison CSV, dated JSON receipt or all-day ICS calendar. The working-day planner uses public holidays, your selected weekend weekdays and extra closure dates, counting each date once. Confirm applicable workplace rules: these community calendars are not statutory or ATIP deadline advice.

title: Retro Screensavers
description: Install animated aquarium and space scenes as Windows screensavers.
requirements: 64-bit Windows; MinGW-w64 on Linux or WSL to build from source

data_info.detail: Two scenes are drawn locally in code, with per-scene animation speed settings.

readme.note: Try either Windows saver with its /s switch, then use Settings to choose a speed saved separately for that scene. Move the mouse or press a key to exit; both files must be installed for both scenes to appear in the Windows picker.

title: PDF Signing Lab
description: Create a signing identity, sign PDFs and inspect signature integrity and certificate trust.
requirements: Linux, Python 3, OpenSSL, pyHanko and Poppler

data_info.detail: Your PDFs are signed locally. The example uses a self-signed certificate, which does not establish a trusted identity.

readme.note: Compare the unsigned and signed samples with pdfsig, then sign your own copy using an encrypted private key. A valid embedded signature can still report an untrusted self-signed issuer; verify the certificate fingerprint separately before trusting a signer’s identity.

title: RTR Sandbox Explorer
description: Try Payments Canada sandbox messages, inspect responses and export redacted exchanges.
requirements: PHP 8.2+ with curl, XML and ZIP; Payments Canada sandbox credentials

data_info.detail: The provider sandbox returns trigger-based test responses and mocked balances; it does not move real money.

readme.note: Start with Test authentication and Heartbeat, then inspect the response status and message fields before trying a payment scenario. HTTP 200 alone does not mean acceptance; exported exchanges redact tokens but can still contain request data you entered.

title: Compose Diff
description: Compare Docker Compose configurations and review exactly what changed.

data_info.detail: Compose YAML or JSON is parsed and compared in your browser; no container, environment or external file is accessed.

readme.note: Compare before and after configurations, narrow the results by service or change type, and export a dated report. Values start hidden in results and exports; reveal them only after checking for secrets, and remember that comments and mapping order are not structural changes.

title: MIME Cabinet
description: Look up media types, interpret Content-Type headers and compare file signatures with their names.

data_info.detail: A bundled mime-db reference and bounded file-header checks run locally; files and pasted headers stay in your browser.

readme.note: Look up **report.docx**, **image/jpeg** or any extension. Shared extensions can return several media types. Paste a Content-Type value to inspect its parameters. For a local file, **Inspect file header** reads at most 64 KiB and keeps extension, browser type and signature as separate observations. A ZIP header can be compatible with an Office file without proving that subtype. Unknown signatures remain unknown; no file is uploaded or executed. **Save inspection JSON** includes the filename and first 64 bytes, so review it before sharing.

title: Fleet Sheet
description: See which TransLink vehicles are out, where a route is bunched, and what changed since the previous capture.

data_info.detail: TransLink’s GTFS-Realtime feeds supply vehicle positions, trip delays and service alerts for each saved capture.

readme.note: Pick a capture, then a route. The closest pair is measured along the saved line when this network file has one, and as the crow flies when it does not. A route missing from a partial capture is not counted as zero.

title: Atlas Canada
description: Inspect Canadian RIPE Atlas traceroutes and possible cross-border routes, with hop locations, network breakdowns and original measurements.

data_info.detail: Daily RIPE Atlas traceroutes from Canadian probes, with hop locations from IPinfo Lite and exchange points from PeeringDB.

readme.note: Choose a capture to inspect possible cross-border routes by probe network or destination. The percentage includes only completed traces with known Canadian endpoints; unanswered hops, unlocated addresses and excluded traces are shown separately. IPinfo geolocation and PeeringDB exchange prefixes can place a router in the wrong country, so the result can overcount or undercount real border crossings. Expand a route and follow its RIPE Atlas measurement link to inspect the evidence.

title: Takedown Watcher
description: Track DNS, registration and HTTP changes for watched domains, with dated evidence and cautious takedown indicators.

data_info.detail: Checks of each watched domain run every six hours on GitHub; the instant check asks Cloudflare DNS and RDAP from your browser.

readme.note: Inspect each target's DNS, registration and HTTP evidence and timeline. Ordinary HTTP errors, missing DNS answers, TLS failures and a missing RDAP record do not prove a takedown or identify who acted. Registry hold statuses identify a registrar/registry role but not its reason. “First indicator after report” appears only after an observed live state and a later hold, suspension message or CDN warning; it is an approximate observation interval, not a confirmed response time. Failed DNS checks retain the previous observation and show the error.

title: Abuse Kit
description: Find who to report a phishing site, scam domain or abusive IP address to, and draft the report.

data_info.detail: Looks up DNS, RDAP registration records and RIPEstat network data from your browser when you search.

readme.note: Enter a domain, URL or public IP to find CDN, registrar and network abuse contacts and build an editable report. Contact order is a useful starting point, not a guarantee of responsibility or response speed; a CDN may conceal the origin host. “Someone else” clears the suggested recipient. Bulk mode extracts IPv4 and IPv6 from logs, skips private/reserved addresses, and exports network/contact results plus lookup failures as CSV. Nothing is sent as a report automatically, and the suspect site is never contacted.

title: Edge Map
description: See which Cloudflare data centre serves your connection over IPv4 and IPv6, whether it is in Canada, and how it changes over time.

data_info.detail: Your browser asks Cloudflare's public /cdn-cgi/trace endpoints which data centre answered.

readme.note: The page asks several Cloudflare endpoints for their /cdn-cgi/trace and shows which data centre (an airport code such as YVR or SEA) answered each one, over IPv4 and IPv6. If Cloudflare locates your IP in Canada but an edge outside Canada answered, it is flagged. Turn on "Remember my results in this browser" and come back over days to see whether your ISP's route to Cloudflare moves; the history stores data centre codes only, never your IP, and can be downloaded as CSV.

title: Backup Ledger
description: Find stale or missing restic backups and review the integrity checks that actually ran.

data_info.detail: Your local restic snapshot metadata and recorded integrity-check results stay on your machine. An optional local timer refreshes inventory hourly.

readme.note: Install locally to compare the newest restic snapshot for each host and path set, flag missing expected backups, and review recorded metadata, full-data or subset integrity checks. A recent snapshot does not prove it can be restored; failed refreshes preserve the previous inventory and display the failure. No snapshot metadata is uploaded to CoolCode.

title: Query Confessional
description: Explore observed DNS queries by device, domain and time in your own dnsmasq logs.
requirements: Linux, Python 3.11+ and access to your own dnsmasq query logs

data_info.detail: Your imported dnsmasq query logs stay on your server. Import captures locally to update the inventory; no public downloads or API keys are needed.

readme.note: Query Confessional turns your own dnsmasq query logs into a private device/domain inventory. Import a log, open the local dashboard, choose a device address, and filter a domain to see when DNS queries were observed. Compare query counts and daily activity, or export matching records to CSV. DNS queries do not prove successful connections, page visits or malicious behavior. Explicit source year/timezone settings are required; reimport unchanged or appended captures at the same path, and avoid overlapping rotations. Requires Linux, Python 3.11+ and access to your own dnsmasq logs.

title: Contaminated Places
description: Find federal contaminated sites across Canada by place, contaminant, status and cleanup stage.

data_info.detail: The official Federal Contaminated Sites Inventory covers Canada and some overseas federal sites, with current reported status, contaminants and cleanup steps.

readme.note: Search Halifax or choose British Columbia, then narrow the results by contaminant, inventory status, management strategy or completed cleanup step. Select a site for its custodian, record date and reported contaminant/media pairs. Download every matching result as CSV, or copy a link to the current search and selected site. Nearby search accepts coordinates or optional browser location permission. Closed records remain searchable; a listing alone is not evidence of present-day danger.
